claims.text: Replacing Mo with Ti in as-cast HfMoTaTiZr will reduce alloy density.
Replacing Mo with Ti will maintain strong room-temperature mechanical performance.
Replacing Mo with Ti will maintain strong high-temperature mechanical performance.
Ti has a lower atomic mass than Mo.
Replacing Mo with Ti will reduce the alloy's lattice parameter.
Replacing Mo with Ti will refine the grain structure.
Replacing Mo with Ti will increase lattice distortion and enhance solid-solution strengthening.
The proposed grain refinement will increase dislocation density and reduce grain size.
Preserved solid-solution strengthening and grain refinement will improve or preserve yield strength.
Preserved solid-solution strengthening and grain refinement will improve or preserve fracture toughness.
The modified alloy will have a density no greater than approximately 9.7 g cm^-3, representing at least a 5% reduction.
The modified alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength of at least 1500 MPa.
The modified alloy will have a yield strength of at least 800 MPa at 1000 °C.
The modified alloy will have a room-temperature fracture toughness of at least 20 MPa m^(1/2).
The modified alloy will have a fracture toughness of at least 15 MPa m^(1/2) at 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm^-3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.
Mechanical testing is proposed from room temperature to 1600 °C at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
The controlled experiment will compare 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% replacement of Mo by Ti, using five samples per level.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 5% density reduction, but the rejection rule falsifies only reductions below 3%; a 3–5% reduction would miss the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.

The predicted room-temperature yield strength is at least 1500 MPa, whereas the rejection rule permits up to a 10% loss from 1600 MPa, or a value as low as 1440 MPa. Thus some outcomes below the stated prediction would not falsify the hypothesis.

At high temperature, the prediction requires at least 800 MPa, whereas the rejection rule based on a 10% reduction from 855 MPa permits approximately 770 MPa. Outcomes between about 770 and 800 MPa would violate the prediction but not the rejection criterion.
The boundary claims coverage through 1600 °C, but the experiment tests only room temperature and 1000 °C, so performance over the upper part of the claimed range cannot be falsified.

The fracture-toughness rejection rule is expressed as a percentage reduction, but no baseline fracture-toughness values are supplied, making that rule operationally undefined despite the absolute predicted thresholds.
